rv.q: Northlight Theatre's production, which could use more pace, doesn't fully exploit the rush of energy to be mined in the writing, but it has a lot of emotional integrity, thanks in no small measure to a very strong cast of actors.
"Selling Kabul" is more than a rip-roaring one-act that will have your heart rate increasing until the final blackout.
Northlight has mounted a moving production of SELLING KABUL worthy of the play's many accolades.
Khoury's script is nothing short of suspenseful perfection.
This play will rock you to your core.
Events are hard to watch but identifying with the characters makes it worthwhile.
The tension slowly but surely ratchets up to the point where a character's muffled scream into a pillow is deafening.
Selling Kabul moves leisurely, but it's an intricating thrill ride of emotional intrigue that provides a gut punch to your emotions — making you wonder, will this family ever see each other again?

Peck, Kamal and Vossoughi play out their deadly game of chess in such a way that we see there are no heroes and villains here, only victims doing anything they can to protect themselves and the ones they love.
This suspenseful drama about family and sacrifice is a must see.
